native_result.HypoB: Urban land use in Catalonia (Barcelona province) at the plot-scale 50 m buffer in 2009 promoted Gardening (ornamental) plant invasion, as shown by /workspace/data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv (632 plots): a partial-Spearman correlation of +0.49 (p<1e-3) between urban land cover and the per-plot count of Gardening-introduced species at 50 m after residualising on cropland, in-habitat Spearman rho(urban,n.gard) of +0.26 in Croplands (p=0.013), +0.35 in Broad-leaved forests (p=0.003), +0.38 in Coastal (p=0.040), +0.26 in Scrublands (p=0.006), and Urban-habitat plots (n=65) hosting both the highest mean n.gard=0.69 and the highest mean n.total=2.32 per plot; the /workspace/data/temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv shows the Gardening share of introductions rose from 16.8% (Before 1500) to 75.2% in 1985-2019 (397 of 528 species, 7-fold rise), and /workspace/data/invasion_success_pathways.csv lists 42 of 81 invasive species (51.9%) as Gardening-introduced — the competing Unintentional pathway is the most numerous in absolute terms (289 vs 169 Gardening) and most enriched in the Urban habitat (mean 1.60/plot), while AgriForest is essentially absent from Urban plots (mean 0.03; only 23 total instances concentrated in Riparian+Croplands).
